recent_posts.title: How Swiggy embedded food ordering inside JioHotstar for IPL season
recent_posts.summary: Swiggy's engineering team built a seamless food ordering experience embedded inside the JioHotstar streaming app for IPL season, allowing users to order food without leaving the cricket stream. The integration involved embedding Swiggy's web app in a WebView, solving cross-company authentication via RSA-encrypted phone number sharing and coordinated SMS OTP auto-reading, redesigning layouts for split-screen viewports (fitting 6 restaurants where 2 showed before), building a dedicated integration playground to catch contract mismatches early, implementing two-layer rate limiting with dedicated infrastructure to handle IPL traffic spikes, and using GTM for cross-company analytics while deliberately excluding it from payment pages. The project was completed in 8 weeks across two companies with separate tech stacks and identity systems.

recent_posts.title: Taming Visual Regressions with Playwright and Docker
recent_posts.summary: A practical walkthrough of building a Visual Regression Testing (VRT) pipeline using Playwright and Storybook for a shared UI component library. The post covers auto-discovering stories via Storybook's index.json, capturing pixel-based screenshots, and the key challenge of OS-dependent snapshot differences between macOS (local) and Linux (CI). The solution uses an official Playwright Docker image to standardize the rendering environment, with OS-specific snapshot directories where only Linux snapshots are committed. The pipeline acts as a mandatory CI gate, blocking merges on unexpected visual diffs.

recent_posts.title: Building On-Device Predictive Autocomplete in React Native
recent_posts.summary: Swiggy's Crew team built an on-device predictive autocomplete system for a conversational concierge app in React Native. The system uses two small AI models totaling ~90MB: a MiniLM-L12 classifier (~30MB, ~80ms) for intent/category detection and a fine-tuned SmolLM2-135M slot extractor (~60MB, ~200ms) for structured field extraction. The classifier uses hierarchical two-phase training and attention pooling, while the slot extractor uses LoRA fine-tuning and GGUF quantization with grammar constraints to guarantee clean output. Both models run entirely on-device with no server calls, achieving ~280ms end-to-end latency and offline support. Models are shipped OTA via chunked parallel downloads with safe versioned swaps, and a feedback loop using production signals drives continuous retraining.

recent_posts.title: The Micro-Frontend Evolution: Why We Traded S3 Behaviors for Module Federation (and What It Cost Us)
recent_posts.summary: Swiggy's engineering team shares how they migrated multiple B2B dashboards from a fragmented S3-per-app architecture to a unified Module Federation 2.0 setup. The post covers the full journey: eliminating ~638 KB of duplicate JavaScript per remote app, solving singleton traps (styled-components loaded twice), synchronizing React Router with TanStack Router via memory history, and implementing a cache-busting strategy for remoteEntry.js. The most complex challenge was migrating thousands of authenticated users to a new domain without forced logouts — solved using a popup window + postMessage approach to bypass browser third-party storage partitioning, rolled out in 4 phases from soft nudge to permanent 301 redirect. Also covers config-driven version pinning for sub-5-minute rollbacks and ImageKit integration for image optimization.

recent_posts.title: How Swiggy reduced build times by 80% through systematic optimization
recent_posts.summary: Swiggy's engineering team reduced build times by up to 80% across multiple repositories through systematic optimization. Key strategies included using tar archives instead of direct file copies to Docker, migrating from npm to Yarn workspaces, parallelizing builds, removing redundant package builds in monorepos, separating SDK publishing into parallel pipelines, and aggressively pruning Git tags (from 300,000 to 1,000) and branches. These changes saved approximately 140 developer hours per week across three major repositories while eliminating build failures caused by race conditions.

recent_posts.title: Scaling Swiggy’s Mobile Ecosystem [1/n]
recent_posts.summary: Swiggy's mobile ecosystem has expanded from a single app to a family of apps (Snacc, Instamart, Toing, Dineout, Crew), creating challenges in maintaining quality, stability, and consistency. The article outlines 12+ key challenges including CI/CD at scale, release management, observability, code reusability, quality guidelines, branching strategy, modularization, stability maintenance, clean boundaries, third-party library management, cost optimization, feature flags, and data security. The solution involves rethinking team organization, standardizing processes, investing in tooling, and building smarter CI/CD pipelines, reusable components, stronger observability frameworks, and scalable experimentation platforms.

recent_posts.title: Enabling Real-Time Business Monitoring with Klaxon
recent_posts.summary: Swiggy leverages Klaxon, an in-house real-time business monitoring and alerting system, to enhance proactive problem-solving and operational efficiency. Klaxon supports diverse alerting channels, flexible alert types, and personalized notifications, using technologies like Apache Kafka and Snowflake. Recent improvements have streamlined operations and lowered costs, with Klaxon playing a vital role in maintaining smooth operations and improving decision-making across Swiggy's teams.

recent_posts.title: Rill State Implementation
recent_posts.summary: Swiggy's Rill platform provides real-time data processing using Apache Flink, supporting SQL-based event streaming and custom code for complex logic. Challenges, such as SQL limitations in historical data processing, are addressed using Flink's State Backend, with solutions involving RocksDB for reliable and fault-tolerant state management.

recent_posts.title: Food for Thought: Swiggy’s Deep Learning Journey!
recent_posts.summary: Swiggy leverages advanced deep learning architectures like MIMO and techniques such as transfer learning to optimize its delivery logistics and improve customer satisfaction. By combining multiple models and using specialized regional models, Swiggy enhances delivery time predictions and operational efficiency, achieving significant improvements in performance and cost savings.

recent_posts.title: Building Rock-Solid ML Systems
recent_posts.summary: Machine learning underpins Swiggy's fast and efficient service. Key ML practices include Exploratory Data Analysis and anomaly detection, sensitivity analysis to identify input variations' effects, Explainable AI to demystify model predictions, and adherence to coding standards. These practices ensure reliable, transparent, and high-quality ML systems that deliver exceptional customer experiences.

top_posts.summary: Swiggy developed Hermes, an in-house generative AI tool, to streamline data access and improve decision-making by converting natural language queries into SQL queries within Slack. Using metadata and user-specific context, Hermes significantly reduces dependency on technical resources and enhances data-driven decision-making across the organization.

top_posts.title: Building Rock-Solid ML Systems
top_posts.summary: Swiggy emphasizes the critical importance of machine learning operational excellence (ML Opex) for the reliability and consistent performance of their systems. Highlighting both pre-deployment and post-deployment phases, they provide best practices for ensuring accurate predictions and robust ML models in dynamic environments. The post covers scenarios like data discrepancies and new product capabilities affecting model performance, and outlines strategies such as exploratory data analysis, sensitivity analysis, shadow modes, fallback mechanisms, and real-time alerts.
